summary: 1955 Ground Observer Corps observation tower beside the Klamath Forest Protective Association headquarters, turned over in 1959; both records list it as gone. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 10x10 observation tower per the 1955 and 1959 Forest Lookouts quotes; a Klamath County list describes a two-story enclosed house
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks it Removed; the Klamath County list marks it Gone. Neither gives a removal date.
facts.agency: Ground Observer Corps and Klamath Forest Protective Association

events.note: Board permission given March 23, 1955; nearing completion in an August 1955 Herald and News item; built through volunteer work and contributions
Used for aircraft observation before effective radar
Turned over to the Klamath Forest Protective Association on January 1, 1959; then usable as a training tower for new lookouts

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1955 article and the 1959 report both call the structure a tower or observation tower, and the 1959 report also calls it a building. The Klamath County list describes a 10x10 two-story enclosed house. The record keeps the 10x10 observation tower wording from the Forest Lookouts quotes and notes the enclosed-house description as a disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Two independent records. Location conflict: Forest Lookouts ties the page to Klamath FPA - 40S-5E-31 (T40S R5E, section 31), while the Klamath County list places the 1955 Ground Observer Corps structure at Sec 7 T39S R9E. The Klamath County list says it was at the KFPA compound, which fits the headquarters, but the section numbers disagree. The brief's coordinates were not checked against either. Form conflict: tower on Forest Lookouts; two-story enclosed house on the Klamath County list. Removal date and method are not documented. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1958 ODF annual report that is not itself in the cache. The brief's agency 'unknown' is replaced with the managing agencies the Klamath County list gives.
